text.p: Severe flooding is ongoing in the US North Plains across many river systems. Cool temperatures for one more day keep snowmelt slow. After that, warmer weather will develop, quickening snowmelt, and may lead to even more severe flooding. Also, flooding conditions are expected to develop in Manitoba, Canada, the next several days as temperatures warm and a heavy snowpack melts.

Typhoon Isa, with 105 mph winds, is near 10n/146e, moving west at 7 mph, about 210 miles south southeast of Guam. Typhoon or near-typhoon conditions are expected in Guam and Rota. Tropical storm conditions are likely on other islands in the vicinity. Shipping is under high risk from this storm system. Isa is expected to peak with top winds over 120 mph during the next 24 hours before a slow weakening trend begins as the storm turns more to the north, west of the islands.
There are no further emergency statements at this time.
